learn.explainer: An account created or used without approval. On a connected camera or recorder, it can allow someone to access or change settings.
Demand that is sustained and established rather than only signaled. In this story, a drone-industry leader says such demand is needed beyond positive signals.
Infrastructure used for energy-related operations. The report says Algerian troops are expected to protect facilities in northern Niger near the Libyan border.

analysis.headline: Authority, demand and infrastructure shape today’s stories
paragraphs: The cyber items raise questions about control and accountability: CERT-UA reports altered camera settings and unauthorized accounts, while an agency guide emphasizes knowing whose authority an AI agent used. Both suggest defenders need reliable records of access and action.

The drone story distinguishes positive signaling from sustained, normalized demand. That distinction sits alongside industry discussions of production and AI integration, suggesting analysts should separate stated intent from demonstrated production requirements.

The Algeria-Niger report places troop deployment around energy facilities near the Libyan border. Across these stories, operational capacity and control are central themes. Watch for clearer evidence of access, sustained demand, and the scope of infrastructure protection.
takeaways: Audit device accounts and settings, and preserve records of agent authority.
Distinguish drone demand signals from sustained requirements.
Track the stated purpose and location of the Niger deployment.
